mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 0.5% compresses equity discount rates, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate continued monetary easing and liquidity support.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >60% of periods when FEDFUNDS <= 0.5% (t-test p>0.05 vs baseline).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.5 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions, triggering negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days as recession risks intensify.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >60% of instances when UNRATE rises >0.5pp (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous month-over-month declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) exceeding 0.5% signal a severe demand collapse, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as economic contraction deepens.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline > 0.5% in 1 month
evidence_refs: fact:HOUST at 505.0 (March 2009) and RSAFS at 324323.0 (April 2009) show recent declines
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in >60% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline >0.5% (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In the post-shock recovery regime, industrial production (INDPRO) below 90 signals stalled economic recovery, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as growth expectations fall.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of post-shock recovery periods when INDPRO < 90 (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month increase in retail sales (RSAFS) signals strengthening consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days as corporate earnings prospects improve.
evidence_refs: fact:RSAFS at 324323.0 (April 2009) shows recent decline but trend is monitored
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in >60% of periods when RSAFS increases (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate falls below 0.5%, it signals aggressive monetary easing, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as liquidity floods the market.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in >60% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 0.5% (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in unemployment (UNRATE) and declines in payroll employment (PAYEMS) exceeding 0.5% month-over-month signal a deteriorating labor market, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as recession risks rise.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.5pp and PAYEMS declines > 0.5% in 1 month
evidence_refs: fact:UNRATE at 9.0% (April 2009) and PAYEMS at 131822.0 (April 2009) show recent deterioration
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of instances when both UNRATE rises >0.5pp and PAYEMS declines >0.5% (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, a federal funds rate above 4.5% signals reduced liquidity, driving negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days as risk assets face higher discount rates.
evidence_refs: fact:Current FEDFUNDS at 0.15% is below 4.5% (mechanism inactive now)
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >60% of monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%) (t-test p>0.05).
